findings.claim: a huge duration count crashed int() and non-ASCII digits were accepted
the r4 and r5 commands did not run the tests they name

verdict.text: Both findings sent back are fixed and the fixes broke nothing nearby.
`loopctl gate stamp` from the worktree: lint, format and tests pass; rows r1 to r6 pass; "stamp green: 0b433448b538bd9e184e94abf4fb9eaa3691f622e20ae24aff5659cc3e8fee5d".
Ran the round 1 edge script again against the worktree.
The 5000-digit count is now refused with the --stale-after message instead of crashing, and `٣d` is refused.
Every other case gives the same result as in round 1.
Six-digit cap: `100y` gives 2126-10-15, `999y` and `999999d` are accepted, and `7973y` reaches 9999-10-15.
`7974y`, `999999w`, `999999m` and `999999y` are refused as too far in the future.
`1000000d` is refused as not a duration.
Every count the plan has in mind (days to a few years) fits easily, and anything the cap cuts off is past year 9999 anyway in every unit except days, where it is past year 4764.
test_stale_after_refused_odd_counts asserts a ConceptError naming --stale-after for the 5000-digit count, the Arabic-Indic digit and a seven-digit count.
It would fail if any of them crashed or were accepted.
The r4 command now runs test_new_freshness_valid by node id plus tests/test_okf_fields.py.
The r5 command runs test_init_block_names_freshness and test_new_freshness_documented by node id.
`_DURATION` is `([0-9]{1,6})([dwmy])` at src/kmctl/concepts.py:51, and the comment above it says why.
The r4 and r5 commands in rows.json name their tests by node id.
